posts.text: This month, we honor those who fought for disability rights, celebrate the strength, creativity, and identity of our disability community, and recognize the barriers that many disabled Marylanders still face – and our responsibility to keep working to remove them.
posts.summary: Honors disability rights, commits to removing barriers for disabled Marylanders

No one should have to justify who they love or how they express themselves.

I’m grateful to have worked alongside LGBTQ+ advocates to make Maryland a safe haven for their community. Together, we’ve passed the Trans Health Care Equity Act, decriminalized HIV, and doubled funding for hate crime prevention – and we’re not done!

posts.text:
The Trump Administration does not get to pick and choose who has the right to be an American.

For generations, the promise that every child born on American soil is an American citizen has been woven into the very fabric of our Constitution. 

Today's ruling affirms that promise.

posts.text:
Today, we honor the five Capital Gazette staffers killed in an attack on their newsroom eight years ago. 

Today is a reminder that we must protect the freedom of the press. A free press allows our journalists to report the truth and serve our democracy by keeping residents informed about our government.
posts.summary: Honors slain journalists, affirms commitment to protecting press freedom

posts.text:
The Howard Street Tunnel project is complete, and it's now open for double-stack rail service – a huge economic win for our state. 

Here's what that means for Marylanders:

☑️ Around 160,000 additional containers moving through the Port every year, 
☑️ about $1 billion in economic benefits for Marylanders annually,
☑️ fewer trucks on our road ways, and 
☑️ over 13,000 new jobs expected — in construction, warehousing, logistics, and port operations

This project started as a $566 million project
